+Role: You are an expert systems programmer specializing in Linux desktop development, GTK4, and browser engine integration.
+
+Task: Build the first iteration of a Linux-native, hybrid-rendering web browser shell called Project Indigo. The project must prioritize a lightweight default engine (WebKitGTK 6.0) with a heavyweight escape hatch (CEF) for complex sites, all managed by a GTK4 native interface. The target environment is Fedora 44 (or later), and the system has 16GB of RAM. Under no circumstances should the build process attempt to compile Chromium, WebKit, or the CEF engine from source. Rely exclusively on system packages for the engines.
+
+1. Core Architecture & Constraints
+
+    Platform: Fedora 44 or later (the development machine runs Fedora 44). The application must be native to Linux; no cross-platform abstractions like Electron.
+
+    UI Framework: GTK4. The shell (tabs, window) must be built with GTK4 widgets.
+
+    Default Rendering Engine: WebKitGTK 6.0. This is the lightweight, default engine for every new tab. It is installed as a system library and must not be built from source.
+
+    Heavy Rendering Engine: Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF). This is the optional, heavyweight engine used only for specific tabs or sites on demand. On Fedora it is available as the system packages `cef` (runtime) and `cef-devel` (headers, FindCEF.cmake, and libcef_dll_wrapper sources). It must not be built from source; only the small `libcef_dll_wrapper` shim is compiled as part of the consumer project.
+
+    Memory Constraint: The entire build and run process must be mindful of a 16GB RAM environment. Avoid any build step that compiles a browser engine. The goal is to write the integration code, not to build the engines. Compiling the `libcef_dll_wrapper` shim is expected and acceptable (it takes a minute or two, not hours).
+
+    Package Verification (do this first): Before generating any build files, run `dnf info gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel cef cef-devel` and confirm each is available. Run `dnf repoquery --qf '%{name} from %{repoid}' cef cef-devel` to note which repository provides CEF (Fedora may source it from a third-party or COPR repo rather than the official Fedora repos). If any required package is missing, STOP and report it to the user. Do NOT substitute a source build, a Spotify CDN download, or a different engine.
+
+2. Required System Packages (Fedora)
+
+The agent must instruct the user to install the following via dnf (the agent itself must not run sudo or modify system packages):
+
+    GTK4 & Build Tools: gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc gcc-c++
+
+    WebKitGTK 6.0: webkitgtk6.0-devel (provides headers and libraries for the GTK4-compatible WebKit API)
+
+    CEF: cef cef-devel (cef-devel provides headers, FindCEF.cmake, and libcef_dll_wrapper source)
+
+    Suggested command: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc gcc-c++ webkitgtk6.0-devel cef cef-devel
+
+Discovery step for CEF paths (do not guess): run `rpm -ql cef-devel | grep -iE 'cmake|wrapper|include'` to locate FindCEF.cmake and the libcef_dll_wrapper sources on this system, and use those paths in the CMake build.
+
+3. Implementation Milestones (First Iteration)
+
+The agent should implement the following milestones in order. The goal is a vertical slice that proves the hybrid architecture is viable, not a fully-featured browser. Deliver Milestone 1 first, stop, and wait for the user's confirmation before proceeding to Milestone 2.
+
+Milestone 1: Minimal GTK4 + WebKitGTK Shell
+
+    Create a GtkApplication and a main window.
+
+    Implement a GtkNotebook as the tab container.
+
+    The default tab content must be a WebKit.WebView (from WebKitGTK 6.0, include <webkit/webkit.h>) loaded with a hardcoded URL (e.g., https://example.com).
+
+    Use pkg-config for flags: `pkg-config --cflags --libs gtk4 webkitgtk-6.0`.
+
+    Goal: Verify that a native GTK4 window can render a web page using the system's WebKitGTK library with zero engine compilation. Provide the minimal meson.build and C source code for this. Target: `meson setup build && ninja -C build && ./build/indigo` opens a window and renders the page.
+
+Milestone 2: Tab Management & Engine Abstraction
+
+    Extend the GtkNotebook to allow opening new tabs (e.g., a "New Tab" button).
+
+    Introduce a lightweight abstraction layer (a simple struct) that represents a Tab. This Tab object must hold a reference to either a WebKitWebView widget or a placeholder for a CEF browser.
+
+    Implement the logic to add and remove tabs from the GtkNotebook dynamically.
+
+Milestone 3: CEF Integration via a Separate Process
+
+    Do not attempt to embed CEF's rendering directly into the GTK window in this first iteration (no OSR, no foreign-widget parenting). Instead, implement the process-isolation model discussed for the hybrid architecture.
+
+    Create a separate, minimal CEF host application (a standalone executable, C++). This host initializes CEF, creates its own native window, and loads a given URL. It should follow the cefsimple example pattern.
+
+    In the main GTK shell, implement an "Open in Full Mode (CEF)" action for the current tab. This action should:
+
+        Spawn the CEF host process as a child.
+
+        Pass the current URL to the CEF process via a command-line argument.
+
+        The main shell should either hide the WebKit view and display the CEF window, or manage it as a separate window for this initial proof-of-concept. The key is that the CEF engine lives in a separate process that can be terminated independently.
+
+    Goal: Prove that the GTK shell can orchestrate a second, heavyweight rendering process without integrating its event loop directly. This mirrors the architecture of FixBrowser, where heavy tabs run in separate processes to manage memory.
+
+4. Code and Project Structure Requirements
+
+    Language: Use C for the GTK/WebKit shell to minimize complexity and build times. Use C++ only for the CEF host process, as required by the CEF C++ API.
+
+    Build System: Use Meson + Ninja for the GTK shell. Use CMake + Ninja for the CEF host, because CMake is required to consume the system-provided FindCEF.cmake. Do not attempt to drive the CEF host through Meson.
+
+    CEF Integration: Use the system FindCEF.cmake from cef-devel. Build only the `libcef_dll_wrapper` static library as part of the CEF host project (via add_subdirectory on the wrapper sources or an equivalent explicit target). Do NOT download prebuilt CEF binaries from Spotify's servers; the system package is the source of truth. Do NOT attempt to build the CEF engine itself.
+
+    Process Management: For the CEF host process, implement the standard CEF multi-process architecture. On Linux, CEF relaunches the host executable itself for subprocesses, passing --type= arguments; set CefSettings.browser_subprocess_path accordingly (or provide a dedicated helper executable). Ensure the host detects the --type= argument and calls CefExecuteProcess before CefInitialize. Handle sandbox configuration explicitly; if the sandbox causes failures on this system, document the no_sandbox fallback rather than silently disabling it.
+
+    Wayland/X11 Risk: CEF's native window path is historically more reliable under X11 than Wayland. For the CEF host, default to running under XWayland (e.g., launch with GDK_BACKEND=x11 if the host uses GTK, or ensure the CEF window is an X11 window). Document this in the README rather than letting the user hit a silent failure.
+
+5. Deliverables
+
+Provide the complete project scaffold, including:
+
+    A README.md with the exact dnf install command, the package-verification commands, and build/run instructions for both components.
+
+    A meson.build file for the GTK shell.
+
+    A CMakeLists.txt for the CEF host process (consuming the system FindCEF.cmake).
+
+    The C source code for the GTK4 shell with the GtkNotebook and WebKitWebView.
+
+    The C++ source code for the minimal CEF host process (based on cefsimple, adapted for the system CEF package).
+
+    Clear instructions on how to build and run both components, and how the shell spawns the CEF host.
+
+6. Working Rules
+
+    You are NOT to publish or commit any changes. Do not run git commit, git push, gh, or publish anything anywhere. Do not create tags, releases, or pull requests. All changes remain local.
+
+    Do not run sudo, do not install packages, and do not modify files outside the project directory. Instruct the user to install packages themselves.
+
+    If a required system package or header is missing, STOP and report the exact missing item. Do not substitute a source build, a CDN download, or a different engine.
+
+    Implement Milestone 1 in full, then stop and wait for confirmation before starting Milestone 2.
+
+7. Critical Constraints (Reiteration)
+
+    NEVER compile WebKitGTK or the CEF engine from source. ONLY use the system packages installed via dnf. The only CEF compilation permitted is the small libcef_dll_wrapper shim.
+
+    NEVER attempt to directly embed the CEF browser window as a child of a GTK widget in this first iteration (no OSR). ALWAYS use a separate process for the CEF engine to ensure stability and memory management.
+
+    The entire build process must fit comfortably within the constraints of a 16GB RAM machine. The goal is to compile only the application's integration code, not the browser engines themselves.

# Project Indigo

Project Indigo is a small native GTK4 browser shell. Its initial milestone opens one WebKitGTK 6.0 web view in a GTK notebook; it does not build a browser engine.

## Fedora dependencies

Install the system libraries and build tools (the project does not install packages):

```sh
sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc gcc-c++ webkitgtk6.0-devel cef cef-devel
```

Check package availability before building:

```sh
dnf info gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel cef cef-devel
dnf repoquery --qf '%{name} from %{repoid}' cef cef-devel
```

CEF is an optional later milestone and is not used or built by this GTK/WebKit shell. Fedora 44 currently provides `cef` and `cef-devel` from the `fedora` and `updates` repositories. CEF host paths and build instructions will be documented only if that later milestone is approved.

## Build and run

From the project root:

```sh
meson setup build
ninja -C build
./build/indigo
```

The shell uses the system `gtk4` and `webkitgtk-6.0` pkg-config dependencies through Meson. The first tab loads `https://example.com`. No engine source is downloaded or compiled.

  'src/main.c',

  install: true,
)
#include <gtk/gtk.h>
#include <webkit/webkit.h>

static void
activate(GtkApplication *application, gpointer user_data)
{
    GtkWidget *window = gtk_application_window_new(application);
    gtk_window_set_title(GTK_WINDOW(window), "Indigo");
    gtk_window_set_default_size(GTK_WINDOW(window), 1100, 760);

    GtkWidget *notebook = gtk_notebook_new();
    gtk_notebook_set_scrollable(GTK_NOTEBOOK(notebook), TRUE);

    GtkWidget *web_view = webkit_web_view_new();
    GtkWidget *tab_label = gtk_label_new("New Tab");
    gtk_notebook_append_page(GTK_NOTEBOOK(notebook), web_view, tab_label);

    gtk_window_set_child(GTK_WINDOW(window), notebook);
    gtk_window_present(GTK_WINDOW(window));

    webkit_web_view_load_uri(WEBKIT_WEB_VIEW(web_view), "https://example.com");
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    GtkApplication *application = gtk_application_new(
        "com.projectindigo.Browser",
        G_APPLICATION_DEFAULT_FLAGS
    );
    g_signal_connect(application, "activate", G_CALLBACK(activate), NULL);

    int status = g_application_run(G_APPLICATION(application), argc, argv);
    g_object_unref(application);
    return status;
}

### SPEC — 5/10
1. [src/main.c](src/main.c) implements the requested single GTK application window, `GtkNotebook`, and default WebKitGTK view loading a hardcoded URL.
2. [meson.build](meson.build) and [README.md](README.md) provide the requested Milestone 1 build path and user setup instructions. The GTK4 and WebKitGTK pkg-config dependency names are consistent with the plan.
3. The README’s install command includes CEF packages even though this milestone neither uses CEF nor builds its host. That is extra setup for the requested first slice; the README itself calls CEF optional.

### DESIGN — 5/10
1. This is a deliberately small one-file application, reasonable for Milestone 1; there is no grown application structure to evaluate yet.
2. [src/main.c](src/main.c) leaves the `activate` callback parameter unnamed. GCC accepts it as an extension in the default language mode, but emits a pedantic warning before C23; naming it and marking it unused would avoid that portability issue.
3. The README says both CEF runtime and development packages are optional later, while its install command requests them now. That makes the setup guidance internally inconsistent.

### CORRECTNESS — 2/10
1. **Runtime behavior is unverified:** GTK4 and WebKitGTK development packages are absent, and pkg-config cannot resolve `gtk4` or `webkitgtk-6.0`.
2. **Build is unverified:** Meson is not installed, so the documented `meson setup build && ninja -C build && ./build/indigo` path could not run.
3. I found no definite GTK4/WebKitGTK API defect from source inspection. `GtkNotebook`, `webkit_web_view_new()`, and `webkit_web_view_load_uri()` are the intended Milestone 1 APIs, but without compiling or running, that is not proof the shell builds or renders.

### QUALITY — 7/10
1. [src/main.c](src/main.c) is concise for the requested shell; there are no additional layers, dead scaffolding, or later-milestone features.
2. The main avoidable overhead is requesting unused CEF packages in the README’s install command.
3. The unnamed callback parameter is a small, avoidable portability warning.

**Most valuable next pass:** Install the GTK4 and WebKitGTK development packages and Meson, then compile and run this exact milestone to confirm the real window and page rendering. That would distinguish any actual source/build defects from the current environment blocker. No files were changed during this audit.

When the dependencies are available, I can build and run the Milestone 1 shell to verify it end to end.

static void
activate(GtkApplication *application, gpointer user_data)
{
    (void)user_data;

    GtkWidget *window = gtk_application_window_new(application);
    gtk_window_set_title(GTK_WINDOW(window), "Indigo");
    gtk_window_set_default_size(GTK_WINDOW(window), 1100, 760);

    GtkWidget *notebook = gtk_notebook_new();
    GtkWidget *web_view = webkit_web_view_new();
    GtkWidget *tab_label = gtk_label_new("Example");
    gtk_notebook_append_page(GTK_NOTEBOOK(notebook), web_view, tab_label);

    g_object_unref(application);
    return status;
}

# Project Indigo

Project Indigo is a small native GTK4 browser shell. Its initial milestone opens one WebKitGTK 6.0 web view in a GTK notebook; it does not build a browser engine.

## Fedora dependencies

Install the system libraries and build tools (the project does not install packages):

```sh
sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc webkitgtk6.0-devel
```

Check package availability before building:

```sh
dnf info gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel
```

## Build and run

From the project root:

```sh
meson setup build
ninja -C build
./build/indigo
```

The shell uses the system `gtk4` and `webkitgtk-6.0` pkg-config dependencies through Meson. The first tab loads `https://example.com`. No engine source is downloaded or compiled.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Indigo test.sh — build and run the Project Indigo development checkout.
#
# Builds the sibling project-indigo source tree with Meson and launches the
# result, so development runs from source rather than a packaged copy.
#
# Usage: ./test.sh [--help]   (INDIGO_SRC=<path> overrides the checkout)
#

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

CYAN='\033[0;36m'
RED='\033[31m'
NC='\033[0m'

msg() { printf '%b\n' "${CYAN}${1}${NC}"; }
die() { printf '%b\n' "${RED}${1}${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  ./test.sh                      Build and run ../project-indigo
  INDIGO_SRC=<path> ./test.sh    Build and run another checkout
  ./test.sh --help               Show this help

The Meson build directory is <source>/build.
EOF
}

# --- Dev source ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Default to the project-indigo checkout beside this repo; override with
# INDIGO_SRC if your development tree lives elsewhere.
DEFAULT_SRC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../project-indigo"
INDIGO_SRC="${INDIGO_SRC:-$DEFAULT_SRC}"

if [ -d "$INDIGO_SRC" ]; then
    INDIGO_SRC="$(cd "$INDIGO_SRC" && pwd)"
fi

BUILD_DIR="${INDIGO_SRC}/build"

check_dev_source() {
    if [ ! -f "${INDIGO_SRC}/meson.build" ] || [ ! -f "${INDIGO_SRC}/src/main.c" ]; then
        die "Error: Project Indigo source not found at:
  ${INDIGO_SRC}

Set INDIGO_SRC to a valid project-indigo checkout."
    fi
}

check_tools() {
    local tool
    for tool in meson ninja; do
        if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            die "Error: '$tool' not found on PATH.
Install the build dependencies: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc webkitgtk6.0-devel"
        fi
    done
}

run_dev() {
    check_dev_source
    check_tools

    if [ -f "${BUILD_DIR}/build.ninja" ]; then
        msg "--- Reconfiguring ${BUILD_DIR} ---"
        meson setup --reconfigure "$BUILD_DIR" "$INDIGO_SRC"
    else
        msg "--- Configuring ${BUILD_DIR} ---"
        meson setup "$BUILD_DIR" "$INDIGO_SRC"
    fi

    msg "--- Building Indigo ---"
    meson compile -C "$BUILD_DIR"

    msg "--- Running Indigo from ${INDIGO_SRC} ---"
    exec "${BUILD_DIR}/indigo"
}

case "${1:-}" in
    "")
        run_dev
        ;;
    -h|--help)
        usage
        ;;
    *)
        die "Unknown option: $1. Use --help for usage."
        ;;
esac

#
# Indigo test.sh — build and run the Project Indigo development checkout.
#
# Builds the sibling project-indigo source tree with Meson and launches the

# Usage: ./test.sh [--help]   (INDIGO_SRC=<path> overrides the checkout)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# --- Colors -------------------------------------------------------------------
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
RED='\033[31m'
NC='\033[0m'

msg() { printf '%b\n' "${CYAN}${1}${NC}"; }
die() { printf '%b\n' "${RED}${1}${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  ./test.sh                      Build and run ../project-indigo
  INDIGO_SRC=<path> ./test.sh    Build and run another checkout
  ./test.sh --help               Show this help

The Meson build directory is <source>/build.
EOF
}

# --- Dev source ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Default to the project-indigo checkout beside this repo; override with
# INDIGO_SRC if the development tree lives elsewhere.
DEFAULT_SRC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../project-indigo"
INDIGO_SRC="${INDIGO_SRC:-$DEFAULT_SRC}"

if [ -d "$INDIGO_SRC" ]; then
    INDIGO_SRC="$(cd "$INDIGO_SRC" && pwd)"
fi

BUILD_DIR="${INDIGO_SRC}/build"

check_dev_source() {
    if [ ! -f "${INDIGO_SRC}/meson.build" ] || [ ! -f "${INDIGO_SRC}/src/main.c" ]; then
        die "Error: Project Indigo source not found at:
  ${INDIGO_SRC}

Set INDIGO_SRC to a valid project-indigo checkout."
    fi
}

check_tools() {
    local tool
    for tool in meson ninja; do
        if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            die "Error: '$tool' not found on PATH.
Install the build dependencies: sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc webkitgtk6.0-devel"
        fi
    done
}

run_dev() {
    check_dev_source
    check_tools

    if [ -f "${BUILD_DIR}/build.ninja" ]; then
        msg "--- Reconfiguring ${BUILD_DIR} ---"
        meson setup --reconfigure "$BUILD_DIR" "$INDIGO_SRC"
    else
        msg "--- Configuring ${BUILD_DIR} ---"
        meson setup "$BUILD_DIR" "$INDIGO_SRC"
    fi

    msg "--- Building Indigo ---"
    meson compile -C "$BUILD_DIR"

    msg "--- Running Indigo from ${INDIGO_SRC} ---"
    exec "${BUILD_DIR}/indigo"
}

case "${1:-}" in
    "")
        run_dev
        ;;
    -h|--help)
        usage
        ;;
    *)
        die "Unknown option: $1. Use --help for usage."
        ;;
esac

#include "browser.h"

static GtkWidget *window;
static GtkWidget *entry;

static GtkWidget *
find_type(GtkWidget *widget, GType type)
{
    if (G_TYPE_CHECK_INSTANCE_TYPE(widget, type))
        return widget;

    for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(widget);
         child != NULL;
         child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
        GtkWidget *found = find_type(child, type);
        if (found != NULL)
            return found;
    }

    return NULL;
}

static void
print_chain(const char *label)
{
    GtkWidget *focus = gtk_root_get_focus(GTK_ROOT(window));
    GtkWidget *popover = find_type(gtk_window_get_child(GTK_WINDOW(window)), GTK_TYPE_POPOVER);

    g_print("%s: focus=%s entry_has_focus=%d popover_visible=%d\n",
            label,
            focus != NULL ? G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(focus) : "(none)",
            gtk_widget_has_focus(entry),
            popover != NULL && gtk_widget_get_visible(popover));

    if (focus != NULL && focus != entry)
        for (GtkWidget *w = focus; w != NULL; w = gtk_widget_get_parent(w))
            g_print("  focus chain: %s\n", G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(w));
}

static gboolean
after_open(gpointer data)
{
    (void)data;

    print_chain("popover open");

    /* What a keystroke would do: GTK delivers key events to the focus widget. */
    GtkWidget *focus = gtk_root_get_focus(GTK_ROOT(window));
    g_print("typing would reach: %s\n",
            focus == NULL ? "(nothing)" : G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(focus));

    gtk_window_destroy(GTK_WINDOW(window));
    return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
}

static void
activate(GtkApplication *application, gpointer data)
{
    (void)data;

    window = browser_window_new(application);
    gtk_window_present(GTK_WINDOW(window));

    entry = find_type(gtk_window_get_child(GTK_WINDOW(window)), GTK_TYPE_ENTRY);
    g_print("entry=%s\n", entry != NULL ? G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(entry) : "(missing)");

    if (entry != NULL) {
        gtk_widget_grab_focus(entry);
        print_chain("after grab_focus");
    }

    g_timeout_add(700, after_open, NULL);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    GtkApplication *application = gtk_application_new(
        "com.projectindigo.FocusProbe", G_APPLICATION_NON_UNIQUE);

    g_signal_connect(application, "activate", G_CALLBACK(activate), NULL);
    int status = g_application_run(G_APPLICATION(application), argc, argv);
    g_object_unref(application);
    return status;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"eaJZtsUUFZ8","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"/tmp/type-control.c","instructions":"Create a minimal XTEST control window with one entry.","content":"#include <gdk/x11/gdkx.h>
#include <gtk/gtk.h>
#include <X11/Xlib.h>
#include <X11/extensions/XTest.h>
#include <X11/keysym.h>

static GtkWidget *entry;

static void
type_text(Display *display, const char *text)
{
    for (const char *p = text; *p != '\0'; p++) {
        char one[2] = { *p, '\0' };
        KeySym keysym = *p == ' ' ? XK_space : XStringToKeysym(one);
        KeyCode code = XKeysymToKeycode(display, keysym);

        XTestFakeKeyEvent(display, code, True, CurrentTime);
        XTestFakeKeyEvent(display, code, False, CurrentTime);
    }

    XFlush(display);
}

static gboolean
start(gpointer data)
{
    GtkWidget *window = data;
    GdkSurface *surface = gtk_native_get_surface(gtk_widget_get_native(window));
    Display *display = XOpenDisplay(NULL);

    g_print("control: active=%d surface=%s\n",
            gtk_window_is_active(GTK_WINDOW(window)),
            G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(surface));

    if (display == NULL || !GDK_IS_X11_SURFACE(surface)) {
        g_print("control: no X display\n");
        return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
    }

    XRaiseWindow(display, gdk_x11_surface_get_xid(surface));
    XSetInputFocus(display, gdk_x11_surface_get_xid(surface), RevertToParent, CurrentTime);
    XFlush(display);
    gtk_widget_grab_focus(entry);

    type_text(display, "abc");
    g_print("control: typed, entry=\"%s\"\n", gtk_editable_get_text(GTK_EDITABLE(entry)));

    g_timeout_add(500, (GSourceFunc)+[] { return G_SOURCE_REMOVE; }, NULL);
    return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
}

static gboolean
report(gpointer data)
{
    g_print("control final: entry=\"%s\"\n",
            gtk_editable_get_text(GTK_EDITABLE(entry)));
    gtk_window_destroy(GTK_WINDOW(data));
    return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
}

static void
activate(GtkApplication *application, gpointer data)
{
    (void)data;

    GtkWidget *window = gtk_application_window_new(application);
    entry = gtk_entry_new();

    gtk_window_set_child(GTK_WINDOW(window), entry);
    gtk_window_set_default_size(GTK_WINDOW(window), 400, 100);
    gtk_window_present(GTK_WINDOW(window));

    g_timeout_add(800, start, window);
    g_timeout_add(1600, report, window);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    GtkApplication *application = gtk_application_new(
        "com.projectindigo.Control", G_APPLICATION_NON_UNIQUE);

    g_signal_connect(application, "activate", G_CALLBACK(activate), NULL);
    int status = g_application_run(G_APPLICATION(application), argc, argv);
    g_object_unref(application);
    return status;
}

static GtkWidget *
find_type(GtkWidget *widget, GType type)
{
    if (G_TYPE_CHECK_INSTANCE_TYPE(widget, type))
        return widget;

    for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(widget);
         child != NULL;
         child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
        GtkWidget *found = find_type(child, type);
        if (found != NULL)
            return found;
    }

    return NULL;
}

static gboolean
report(gpointer data)
{
    GtkWidget *window = data;
    GtkWidget *root = gtk_window_get_child(GTK_WINDOW(window));
    GtkWidget *popover = find_type(root, GTK_TYPE_POPOVER);
    GtkWidget *entry = find_type(root, GTK_TYPE_ENTRY);
    GtkWidget *focus = gtk_root_get_focus(GTK_ROOT(window));

    g_print("startup: window_active=%d\n", gtk_window_is_active(GTK_WINDOW(window)));

                surface != NULL ? G_OBJECT_TYPE_NAME(surface) : "(none)");

    gtk_window_destroy(GTK_WINDOW(window));
    return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
}

Implemented. The browser now has a real new tab page, persistent history, and the top-right menu with a separate history panel.

**New tab page** ([pages.c](src/pages.c)). Every new tab — including the first one — opens an internal page at `indigo://newtab` rendered as HTML: a centered grid of large rounded tiles with a monogram, the site title under it clamped to two lines, and the URL as the tooltip. Tiles come from the most-visited URLs in history (top 15, by visit count); until there is history the page shows a "Suggested" row of six common sites. Clicking a tile navigates in that tab.

**History** ([history.c](src/history.c)). One entry per URL with visit count and last-visit time, most recent first, recorded on `WEBKIT_LOAD_FINISHED` for `http(s)` only, so `indigo://` pages and blank documents never pollute it. Persisted to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/history` as tab-separated `last_visit / visits / url / title` lines (titles sanitized to one line), capped at 500 entries. The store owns its own file I/O and exposes reads only — no observers, no callbacks; consumers rebuild when they open.

**Menu** ([menu.c](src/menu.c)). A hamburger `GtkMenuButton` at the right of the toolbar opens a popover with **Settings** and **History**. Settings loads a placeholder page (`indigo://settings`, body text `settings`). History opens a **second popover** with the header *History*, then "Recently closed tabs" (in-memory, last 10, click reopens in a new tab), a **Clear History** button (disabled when empty), and "Recent history" rows with favicon-substitute icon, title and host — clicking a row navigates the current tab. Closed tabs are recorded in [browser.c](src/browser.c) before the notebook page is removed; internal pages are skipped.

**Shared plumbing**: internal pages are loaded with `webkit_web_view_load_html` and an `indigo://` base URI ([pages.h](src/pages.h)); the address bar shows blank for them; a small [util.c](src/util.c) owns `uri_host`, replacing the copy that lived in the omnibox. `meson.build` and the README were updated to match.

**Tradeoffs left open:** tiles use generated monograms rather than real favicons (WebKit's favicon database is per-profile and async; wiring it in would add meaningful machinery); the new tab page is generated at tab creation, so it does not refresh live if history changes while it is open; history keeps one row per URL with a count rather than one row per visit. {"kind":"tool","id":"eh6PGUZJ2gI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"/tmp/indigo-stress.c","instructions":"Stress harness that hammers the menu, history panel and tab controls.","content":"#include <gtk/gtk.h>
#include <webkit/webkit.h>

#include "browser.h"

static GtkWidget *window;
static GtkNotebook *notebook;
static int step;

static GtkWidget *
find_label(GtkWidget *widget, const char *text)
{
    if (GTK_IS_LABEL(widget) &&
        g_strcmp0(gtk_label_get_text(GTK_LABEL(widget)), text) == 0)
        return widget;

    for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(widget); child != NULL;
         child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
        GtkWidget *found = find_label(child, text);

        if (found != NULL)
            return found;
    }

    return NULL;
}

static GtkWidget *
find_type(GtkWidget *widget, GType type)
{
    if (G_TYPE_CHECK_INSTANCE_TYPE(widget, type))
        return widget;

    for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(widget); child != NULL;
         child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
        GtkWidget *found = find_type(child, type);

        if (found != NULL)
            return found;
    }

    return NULL;
}

static GtkWidget *
find_button(GtkWidget *root, const char *text)
{
    GtkWidget *label = find_label(root, text);

    if (label == NULL)
        return NULL;

    for (GtkWidget *widget = label; widget != NULL; widget = gtk_widget_get_parent(widget)) {
        if (GTK_IS_BUTTON(widget))
            return widget;
    }

    return NULL;
}

static void
click(GtkWidget *button, const char *what)
{
    if (button == NULL) {
        g_print("round=%d MISSING %s\n", step, what);
        return;
    }

    g_signal_emit_by_name(button, "clicked");
}

static GtkWidget *
menu_popover(void)
{
    GtkWidget *menu_button = find_type(window, GTK_TYPE_MENU_BUTTON);

    return menu_button != NULL
        ? GTK_WIDGET(gtk_menu_button_get_popover(GTK_MENU_BUTTON(menu_button)))
        : NULL;
}

static GtkWidget *
open_menu(void)
{
    GtkWidget *popover = menu_popover();

    if (popover != NULL && !gtk_widget_get_visible(popover))
        gtk_popover_popup(GTK_POPOVER(popover));

    return popover;
}

static void
close_popovers(void)
{
    GtkWidget *menu = menu_popover();
    GtkWidget *entry = find_type(window, GTK_TYPE_ENTRY);

    if (menu != NULL && gtk_widget_get_visible(menu))
        gtk_popover_popdown(GTK_POPOVER(menu));

    if (entry != NULL) {
        for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(entry); child != NULL;
             child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
            if (GTK_IS_POPOVER(child) && gtk_widget_get_visible(child))
                gtk_popover_popdown(GTK_POPOVER(child));
        }
    }
}

static gboolean
tick(gpointer data)
{
    (void)data;

    switch (step % 8) {
    case 0: {
        GtkWidget *popover = open_menu();

        click(popover != NULL ? find_button(popover, "History") : NULL, "History");
        break;
    }
    case 1:
        click(find_button(window, "Clear History"), "Clear History");
        break;
    case 2: {
        /* Closed tabs and history rows are buttons carrying a url. */
        GtkWidget *row = NULL;
        GtkWidget *stack[256];
        int top = 0;

        stack[top++] = window;
        while (top > 0 && row == NULL) {
            GtkWidget *widget = stack[--top];

            if (GTK_IS_BUTTON(widget) &&
                g_object_get_data(G_OBJECT(widget), "url") != NULL)
                row = widget;

            for (GtkWidget *child = gtk_widget_get_first_child(widget); child != NULL;
                 child = gtk_widget_get_next_sibling(child)) {
                if (top < 256)
                    stack[top++] = child;
            }
        }

        click(row, "history row");
        break;
    }
    case 3:
        close_popovers();
        break;
    case 4: {
        GtkWidget *popover = open_menu();

        click(popover != NULL ? find_button(popover, "Settings") : NULL, "Settings");
        break;
    }
    case 5: {
        close_popovers();
        click(gtk_notebook_get_action_widget(notebook, GTK_PACK_END), "new tab");
        break;
    }
    case 6: {
        int pages = gtk_notebook_get_n_pages(notebook);

        if (pages > 1) {
            GtkWidget *label = gtk_notebook_get_tab_label(
                notebook, gtk_notebook_get_nth_page(notebook, pages - 1));
            GtkWidget *close = find_type(label, GTK_TYPE_BUTTON);

            click(close, "close last tab");
        }
        break;
    }
    case 7:
        close_popovers();
        break;
    }

    step++;

    if (step >= 64) {
        g_print("DONE %d rounds\n", step);
        return G_SOURCE_REMOVE;
    }

    return G_SOURCE_CONTINUE;
}

static void
activate(GtkApplication *application, gpointer data)
{
    (void)data;

    window = browser_window_new(application);
    notebook = GTK_NOTEBOOK(find_type(window, GTK_TYPE_NOTEBOOK));
    gtk_window_present(GTK_WINDOW(window));
    g_timeout_add(80, tick, NULL);
}

int
main(void)
{
    GtkApplication *application = gtk_application_new("com.projectindigo.Stress",
                                                      G_APPLICATION_NON_UNIQUE);
    g_signal_connect(application, "activate", G_CALLBACK(activate), NULL);

    char *argv[] = { "indigo-stress", NULL };
    int status = g_application_run(G_APPLICATION(application), 1, argv);

    g_object_unref(application);
    return status;
}

{
    GtkWidget *stack[512];
    int top = 0;

    stack[top++] = root;

    while (top > 0) {
        GtkWidget *widget = stack[--top];

        if (GTK_IS_LABEL(widget) &&
            g_strcmp0(gtk_label_get_text(GTK_LABEL(widget)), text) == 0) {
            for (GtkWidget *w = widget; w != NULL; w = gtk_widget_get_parent(w)) {

static gboolean
check(GtkIconTheme *theme, const char *name, int size, const char *out)

    GtkIconPaintable *p = gtk_icon_theme_lookup_icon(theme, name, NULL, size, 1,

**Indigo** is a small browser shell: WebKitGTK 6.0 renders the pages and GTK 4
draws everything around them. It does not build or ship an engine of its own.

It opens pages in notebook tabs with back, forward and reload, an address bar
that lists open tabs and recent searches, a native GTK new tab page with the
sites you visit most, browsing history, recently closed tabs, and a main menu.
Internal pages (`indigo://settings`) stay inside the shell.

Private build & release tooling for [Project Indigo](../project-indigo), which
holds only the source. This repo builds, signs and uploads the packages; the
**Nebuff Repo** (`repo.nebuff.xyz`) serves them, and `NebuffRepo` owns the index
and the pages.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `publish.sh` | **Start here.** Bump, build, sign, upload, deploy, verify |
| `development/test.sh` | Dev helper: build and run the source checkout locally |
| `dist/` | Build output, gitignored (uploaded to the shared pool) |

## Publish a release

```sh
./publish.sh 0.1.0
./publish.sh 0.1.0 --dry-run     # read-only checks + the plan
./publish.sh 0.1.0 --no-deploy   # upload only; run NebuffRepo's deploy later
```

The version is `X.Y.Z` and lives in exactly one place: the `version:` argument
of `project()` in `../project-indigo/meson.build`. `publish.sh` writes the
version you pass there, then uses it for every package filename. Commit that
one-line bump with the release.

One run:

1. validates the version, source checkout, signing key, repo page and SSH
   access to `sanas`;
2. builds the app inside one container per target, so each package links the
   libraries that distribution actually ships:
   - **Fedora 44** — `indigo-<version>-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm` (signed)
   - **Debian 13** — `indigo_<version>-1_amd64.deb`
   - **Arch** — `indigo-<version>-1-x86_64-<sha256:12>.pkg.tar.zst` (signed)
   - a portable `indigo-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` + `SHA256SUMS(.asc)`
3. uploads into `sanas:/home/nebuff/aero-repo/www/repo/{rpm,deb,arch,releases}`
   (additive — other projects and older Indigo versions are left alone);
4. runs `../NebuffRepo/bin/deploy.sh`, which rebuilds the signed indexes, the
   page and `versions.json`, then checks the live URLs.

Runtime dependencies are declared in every package, so installing Indigo pulls
in the toolkit and engine it needs:

| Format | Requires |
|---|---|
| rpm | `gtk4`, `webkitgtk6.0` |
| deb | `libgtk-4-1`, `libwebkitgtk-6.0-4` |
| pacman | `gtk4`, `webkitgtk-6.0` |

## Install (what users run)

```sh
curl -sSL https://install.nebuff.xyz/indigo | bash   # adds the signed repo and installs

Typing filters both lists. Pressing Enter either navigates to a URL or host name, or runs a Google search when the text is a query. It does not build a browser engine. ## Fedora dependencies Install the system libraries and build tools (the project does not install packages): ```sh sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc webkitgtk6.0-devel ``` Check package availability before building: ```sh dnf info gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel ``` ## Build and run From the project root: ```sh meson setup build ninja -C build ./build/indigo ``` The shell uses the system `gtk4` and `webkitgtk-6.0` pkg-config dependencies through Meson. The logo is compiled into the binary as a GResource, so the icon in the dock and on the new tab page works from the build tree; `meson install` also installs it into the hicolor theme together with a desktop entry, letting the app appear in your launcher. The first tab, and every new tab, opens a native GTK new tab page: the logo, and a grid of the sites you visit most (a few suggested sites until there is history). Clicking a tile opens the site, and Back returns to the new tab page from the first site you visit in a tab. Tab labels follow the page title, and each tab has its own history and close button. Clicking the address bar (or its search icon) opens a list of open tabs, followed by recent searches. Typing filters both lists. Pressing Enter either navigates to a URL or host name, or runs a Google search when the text is a query. Recent searches are stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/search-history`. The button at the right of the toolbar opens the main menu. **History** opens a submenu with recently closed tabs, **Clear History**, and the sites you visited, newest first; **Settings** opens a placeholder page. Browsing history is stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/history`, one tab-separated line per URL (`last visit`, `visits`, `url`, `title`). Internal pages (`indigo://newtab`, `indigo://settings`) and closed internal tabs are not recorded. It opens WebKitGTK 6.0 pages in GTK notebook tabs, with back/forward/reload controls, an address bar, a new tab page, browsing history, and a main menu. It does not build a browser engine. ## Fedora dependencies Install the system libraries and build tools (the project does not install packages): ```sh sudo dnf install gtk4-devel meson ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config gcc webkitgtk6.0-devel ``` Check package availability before building: ```sh dnf info gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel ``` ## Build and run From the project root: ```sh meson setup build ninja -C build ./build/indigo ``` The shell uses the system `gtk4` and `webkitgtk-6.0` pkg-config dependencies through Meson. The logo is compiled into the binary as a GResource, so the icon in the dock and on the new tab page works from the build tree; `meson install` also installs it into the hicolor theme together with a desktop entry, letting the app appear in your launcher. The first tab, and every new tab, opens a native GTK new tab page: the logo, and a grid of the sites you visit most (a few suggested sites until there is history). Clicking a tile opens the site, and Back returns to the new tab page from the first site you visit in a tab. Tab labels follow the page title, and each tab has its own history and close button. Clicking the address bar (or its search icon) opens a list of open tabs, followed by recent searches. Typing filters both lists. Pressing Enter either navigates to a URL or host name, or runs a Google search when the text is a query. Recent searches are stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/search-history`. The button at the right of the toolbar opens the main menu. **History** opens a submenu with recently closed tabs, **Clear History**, and the sites you visited, newest first; **Settings** opens a placeholder page. Browsing history is stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/history`, one tab-separated line per URL (`last visit`, `visits`, `url`, `title`). Internal pages (`indigo://newtab`, `indigo://settings`) and closed internal tabs are not recorded. The same reasoning keeps this here instead of in a * separate file: the activation path is the browser’s, and clicking * the browser’s new-tab button is the activation path. */ g_signal_connect(app, "activate", G_CALLBACK(activate), NULL); g_application_run(G_APPLICATION(app), argc, argv); g_object_unref(app); return 0; } /* Reflexive helpers that let the application stay a blank slate without * escalating into a second entry point. The logo is compiled into the binary as a GResource, so the icon in the dock and on the new tab page works from the build tree; `meson install` also installs it into the hicolor theme together with a desktop entry, letting the app appear in your launcher. The first tab, and every new tab, opens a native GTK new tab page: the logo, and a grid of the sites you visit most (a few suggested sites until there is history). Clicking a tile opens the site, and Back returns to the new tab page from the first site you visit in a tab. Tab labels follow the page title, and each tab has its own history and close button. + +Clicking the address bar (or its search icon) opens a list of open tabs, followed by recent searches. Typing filters both lists. Pressing Enter either navigates to a URL or host name, or runs a Google search when the text is a query. Recent searches are stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/search-history`. + +The button at the right of the toolbar opens the main menu. **History** opens a submenu with recently closed tabs, **Clear History**, and the sites you visited, newest first; **Settings** opens a placeholder page. Browsing history is stored in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/indigo/history`, one tab-separated line per URL (`last visit`, `visits`, `url`, `title`). Internal pages (`indigo://newtab`, `indigo://settings`) and closed internal tabs are not recorded. No engine source is downloaded or compiled.
